newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef trading was generally higher on fairly good demand and mostly moderate offerings during the week ended Thursday, USDA said in its weekly carlot beef report.

Much improved retail demand for immediate needs was noted for the coming weeks stimulated by early week demand from neighboring NAFTA provinces. This demand was mainly for the Select product, which experienced the higher price gains for the trading week.
Rib and chuck cuts traded higher with the most price advances on the Select cuts.
The round and loin cuts experienced somewhat the same conditions with choice cuts firm while the select cuts generally higher.

Closely trimmed items traded higher, with the most advances on the chuck and round cuts with fairly good demand. Beef trimmings traded higher on good mid-week demand and offerings were mostly moderate.

Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items traded higher on moderate demand and offerings. For the week Select and Choice rib primal $4.00 to $5.00 higher; Select and Choice chuck primal $2.00 to $4.00 higher.

Select and Choice round primal $2.50 to $3.00 higher; select and choice loin primal $1.50 to $2.50 higher; closely trimmed items $1.50 to $3.00 higher; Beef trimmings $2.50 higher; fed cattle and blended coarse ground items steady to $4.00 higher.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses were up $1.39 at $100.86 per cwt ; 700/850 up $1.75 at $100.91; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses up $3.90 at $96.99; 700/850 up $3.24 at $96.27.
